I'm currently analyzing the year-over-year U.S. core inflation rates from January 2015 through December 2016, specifically looking at the monthly data points. This involves a close examination of the figures to understand their movement.

I am now meticulously calculating the year-over-year core inflation rates for the US, focusing on the 2015 to 2016 period. My progress involves deriving these figures from the underlying monthly index data.

I am now compiling the raw monthly index data for U.S. core inflation, specifically from January 2014 through December 2016. This is essential for accurately calculating the year-over-year rates requested for the 2015-2016 period.

**Calculating Inflation Rates**

I am now calculating the year-over-year core inflation rates for the US from January 2015 to December 2016. My current focus is on deriving these percentages from the underlying monthly index data.

**Analyzing Inflation Metrics**

I am now focusing on the year-over-year US core inflation rates from the first half of 2016. My current work involves scrutinizing the month-over-month changes within this specific segment.
[/Thinking]

Of course. Here is the year-over-year (YoY) U.S. core inflation rate from January 2015 to December 2016.

The data represents the percentage change in the **Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items Less Food and Energy (Core CPI)** from the same month in the prior year. The source is the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
